rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent abnormal thoughts or behaviour conditions / all rules (trigger)
rule_level_problems.problem: Every rule is anchored on (or Abnormal behavior, Disturbance in thinking), but neither concept is a common symptom or warning sign per the house standard, and the natural warning-sign entry point, Aggressive behavior, is NOT a SNOMED descendant of Abnormal behavior (checked with is_a), nor are Hallucinations a descendant of Disturbance in thinking. Unless the VHA intake records one of these two concepts, nothing fires on this page. Needs a remaining-questions note and ideally an extra trigger (e.g. Aggressive behavior, or a broad possible pre-screen as on the gold page).

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: abnormal thoughts or behaviour of sudden or recent onset
rule_level_problems.problem: The six 'likely' diagnoses (delirium, mania, psychosis, stimulant intoxication, alcohol intoxication, withdrawal, poisoning) sit inside the red box under 'Manage urgently', yet the priority rule fires only on the Sudden/Recent onset qualifiers. A patient recorded with Abnormal behavior (no onset qualifier) + Fluctuation of level of consciousness + temperature 39 gets probable Delirium but no Urgent priority. The house standard says to reference (active_condition X) for likely diagnoses named in the red box; adding the seven active_condition alternates to the priority rule's 'or' would close this.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable stimulant drug intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rule_level_problems.problem: The comma list is encoded as a flat 'or', so a single non-specific finding (Nausea, which is a common symptom; Sweating; Restlessness; or a BP of 140/90 alone) plus abnormal behaviour yields a PROBABLE stimulant intoxication. Nausea, Sweating and Restlessness are also withdrawal findings, so the same patient is simultaneously probable withdrawal if any stopped/decreased finding is present. The page shows a cluster; any2 (available in the language) would be a more faithful reading. The same flat-'or' choice in the mania and alcohol-intoxication rules is less harmful because those findings are specific.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable stimulant drug intoxication (pulse measurement)
rule_level_problems.problem: Pulse is compared via (measurement (snomed_concept "Pulse, function" "observable entity") bpm). SNOMED also has Heart rate (observable entity); whichever concept VHA records as the routine vital is the only one that will ever match. The gold page gives no precedent for pulse. Worth confirming against the recorded vital, otherwise the 'pulse >= 100' arm is dead.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible dementia in abnormal thoughts or behaviour / check_for
rule_level_problems.problem: The four dementia findings are in check_for but are consumed only inside (onset ...) wrappers in a possible rule. Evidence matching in the house tests is by exact s-expression string, so if the wrapped form does not count as 'used as evidence' the gate will flag four CHECKED FOR BUT NEVER USED items. Also, Difficulty coping is the wrong concept for functional decline (see p36-out-e02).

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent abnormal thoughts or behaviour conditions (Restlessness)
rule_level_problems.problem: Restlessness is checked for twice, plain (for stimulant intoxication) and with the Severe qualifier (for withdrawal). Both are consumed, so the gate passes, but the health worker is asked the same question twice; the unqualified form in the stimulant rule would match the severe recording only if the runtime treats qualified findings as descendants of the plain one.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: abnormal thoughts or behaviour of sudden or recent onset (structure)
rule_level_problems.problem: The outer conjunct (plain Abnormal behavior / Disturbance in thinking) is redundant with the qualified alternates; if runtime matching of a qualified recording against an unqualified pattern is exact rather than subsuming, the rule needs two separate recordings before it fires. Harmless if qualifiers subsume; worth a check.

summary: The page's triage and all seven 'likely' conclusions plus stroke/TIA and dementia are encoded with the right rule types and correct thresholds; the most consequential concern is that nothing anchors the page: the trigger concepts (Abnormal behavior, Disturbance in thinking) are not recorded symptoms or warning signs and Aggressive behavior is not a descendant of either, so the rules may never fire in VHA. Next, the Urgent priority ignores the six likely diagnoses inside the red box and the stimulant rule fires on a single non-specific finding (Nausea or Sweating). Element gaps are small: 'reckless' (mania), 'disorganised behaviour' (psychosis), 'reduced' drug intake (withdrawal), 'asymmetric' (stroke), and Difficulty coping is the wrong concept for the dementia functional-decline criterion.
